---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ROA Information Ratio
EXPRESSION: RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: A given average level of operating profitability is worth more when it is delivered with low year-to-year dispersion, because stable profits signal durable competitive advantage rather than a transient windfall, and investors underreact to the persistence dimension.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The numerator is the profitability theme (smoothed operating ROA) and the denominator is the quality theme (earnings instability), so the score is a profit-per-unit-of-earnings-risk statistic rather than either theme alone. Firms with equal mean ROA are separated by the reliability of that ROA, which is exactly the durable-versus-transient distinction. Standardizing profitability by its own volatility also mutes outlier one-off profit spikes that drive weak sorts on raw ROA.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Cash Backed Operating Profit
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: High reported operating profitability is only informative about future returns when it is matched by actual cash generation; accrual-heavy profits mean-revert and are systematically overpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The first channel is the pure profitability level (EBIT-style operating income over assets) and the second is the accrual-quality channel (earnings less operating cash flow, sign-flipped so cash-backed firms score high). Combining ranks makes the signal long high-profit/low-accrual firms and short low-profit/high-accrual firms, capturing an interaction that neither profitability nor accruals delivers alone. It directly implements "durable operating strength" as profit that has already converted into cash.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Solvency Gated Gross Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross profitability predicts returns mainly in firms whose balance sheets can fund and sustain operations; in liquidity-stressed firms the same gross margin is a distress artifact that will be consumed by creditors rather than accruing to equity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gate is a pure quality/solvency condition (positive net working capital relative to total liabilities) applied multiplicatively to the profitability rank, so profitability only "counts" for financially healthy firms. This is a genuine conditional interaction: the same profitability level maps to different signal values depending on financial health. It should sharpen the long leg toward self-funding profitable firms and push fragile high-margin names out of the top bucket.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Persistence Weighted Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(ib, 0), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability that has been continuously positive over a multi-year window reflects a repeatable business model; the market prices the current profit level but underweights the track record of never losing money.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The profitability theme provides the smoothed operating ROA magnitude while the quality theme provides a persistence count of profitable years, and the product rewards firms that are simultaneously highly and habitually profitable. A firm with one strong year but past losses is heavily discounted, which is the durable-versus-transient separation the story requires. The count is a coarse, robust quality measure that is much less outlier-sensitive than volatility estimates.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Improving Profits With Earned Capital
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), RATIO(re, at))
HYPOTHESIS: An upward trend in operating profitability is credible when the firm has a deep stock of retained earnings, since cumulative internally generated capital verifies that past profits were real and reinvestable rather than one-time or externally financed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: TREND captures the profitability-improvement channel while retained earnings over assets is a balance-sheet quality/maturity measure of accumulated earnings history, so the pair distinguishes a genuine profitability ramp from a fragile turnaround at a capital-depleted firm. Neither leg alone contains this validation logic: young cash-burning firms can trend upward from a very low base, and mature high-RE firms can be stagnant. The rank combination keeps both channels on a comparable scale and preserves broad coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Interest Adjusted Profit With Debt Coverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability net of the cost of debt, combined with the ability of operating cash flow to service total liabilities, isolates operating strength that belongs to shareholders rather than profitability that is manufactured or claimed by leverage.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The first rank is a profitability spread after financing costs (profitability theme adjusted for the capital structure claim) and the second is a cash-flow-to-liabilities solvency ratio (quality theme), so the product is high only when profits survive interest and cash flow comfortably covers obligations. This penalizes the classic levered-ROE illusion, where high equity returns simply reflect debt amplification. It should produce a long leg of unlevered, cash-generative compounders and a short leg of levered, cash-poor firms.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE ROA Information Ratio---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is essentially the well-documented earnings-volatility/earnings-stability anomaly repackaged as a profitability information ratio, and the construction is mechanically fragile because a negative mean ROA divided by a tiny volatility produces huge negative outliers while a loss-making but stable firm and a profitable but stable firm are scored on incomparable scales.

---CRITIQUE Cash Backed Operating Profit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a straight additive rank blend of two of the most heavily published anomalies (Novy-Marx operating profitability and Sloan total accruals) with no genuine conditioning or interaction, so it mostly rediscovers known effects rather than testing a new cross-theme mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Solvency Gated Gross Profitability---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The binary gate does not implement the stated hypothesis — instead of making profitability "not count" for fragile firms, it forces every firm failing the working-capital test to the absolute bottom of the score, so the short leg becomes a pure low-liquidity/distress portfolio and the signal is largely a solvency indicator wearing a profitability label.

---CRITIQUE Persistence Weighted Profitability---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The economic story is reasonable but the multiplicative form on a signed, unbounded ROA is broken at the zero crossing — chronic loss-makers get a count of zero and therefore a score of exactly 0, ranking them above firms with mildly negative smoothed ROA and some profitable years, which inverts the intended ordering in the short leg.

---CRITIQUE Improving Profits With Earned Capital---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Both legs lean on known effects (profitability trend and retained-earnings-to-assets), but the pairing is a coherent and non-obvious validation mechanism, the rank aggregation keeps scales comparable and coverage broad, and the expected positive sign matches the expression's natural direction.

---CRITIQUE Interest Adjusted Profit With Debt Coverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The two-rank product is well-behaved and the interest-adjusted profit crossed with cash-flow debt coverage is a defensible cross-theme construct, though the reasoning's appeal to the "levered-ROE illusion" is inconsistent with an asset-scaled numerator and the second leg partially duplicates the profitability channel it is supposed to validate.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Trough Tested Operating Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Current operating profitability is durable only if the firm stayed solidly profitable in its worst year of the last five; a high profit floor, not symmetric earnings dispersion, is what distinguishes a protected franchise from a cyclical windfall.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Replacing the volatility denominator with a downside floor removes the mechanical fragility of dividing a signed mean by a near-zero standard deviation, and both legs are mapped into bounded cross-sectional ranks so loss-making and profitable firms are scored on one comparable scale. The interaction is genuine: the same current EBITDA/assets is up-weighted only when the five-year minimum net-income-to-assets is also high, so cyclical peakers and firms with a recent loss year are pushed out of the long leg. This is a downside-persistence concept rather than the standard earnings-volatility anomaly, and it needs no outlier winsorization to behave.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Worst Of Accrual And Cash Profitability
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_ADJ(RATIO(oancf, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is only genuinely profitable if it looks profitable on both the accrual and the cash measure relative to its industry; the binding weaker of the two measures is the honest estimate of operating strength, and the market anchors instead on the more flattering one.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The MIN operator is a strictly non-additive conditioning device: a high score is impossible unless accrual profitability and cash profitability are simultaneously strong, so the signal cannot be reproduced by any weighted sum of Novy-Marx profitability and Sloan accruals. Industry adjustment puts the two channels on a common, capital-intensity-neutral footing so the minimum is economically meaningful rather than driven by depreciation or working-capital conventions. Firms whose reported profits outrun cash generation are automatically scored by their cash number, and vice versa, which is exactly the durable-versus-manufactured distinction.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Liquidity Reinforced Gross Profitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), MUL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross profitability is priced too weakly when the firm can self-fund its operating cycle; solvency should amplify the profitability signal rather than define the short leg, since illiquid firms with weak margins, not illiquid firms per se, are the losers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The first channel preserves the full cross-sectional ordering of gross profitability for every firm, so no company is forced to the bottom purely for failing a working-capital test; the second channel gives extra credit that scales with profitability but only accrues to firms with positive net working capital relative to total liabilities. The result is a graded interaction in which the healthy-firm profitability slope is steeper than the fragile-firm slope, which is what the hypothesis actually claims. The short leg is therefore populated by low-margin firms regardless of liquidity, avoiding a pure distress portfolio.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Rank Space Persistent Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(ib, 0), 5)))
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
HYPOTHESIS: Investors price the current level of profitability but underweight the track record behind it, so firms that are both highly profitable now and profitable in every one of the last five years earn abnormal returns relative to equally profitable firms with a broken history.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Ranking the smoothed operating ROA before multiplying removes the zero-crossing pathology of the original form: chronic loss-makers now score near the bottom on both bounded rank channels instead of collapsing to exactly zero and jumping above mildly unprofitable firms. Monotonicity in each argument is preserved, and the product still requires both high current profitability and a full history of positive earnings to reach the top decile. The persistence count is coarse and outlier-immune, so it complements rather than duplicates level-based profitability measures.
